The genome is the complete set of genetic material—DNA or RNA—in an organism, including all of its genes and noncoding sequences. It contains the hereditary information needed to build and maintain that organism. The note’s claim that the term was introduced in the 1990s and applies only to complex multicellular organisms is incorrect; the term dates to 1920 and applies to all organisms, including viruses and bacteria.  
CONFIDENCE: 100
